chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who made it upon himself to fast for a month, and he fasted fifteen days of it, then an event occurred. He said: 'If he fasted fifteen days, he may make up what remains of it; and if he fasted less than fifteen days, it is not sufficient for him until he fasts a complete month.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up a vowed month of fasting if interrupted before completing it?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the 'half-month' threshold for the validity of partial fasting in vow fulfillment, a principle widely adopted in Shia jurisprudence. It distinguishes between a valid partial discharge (requiring only the balance) and an invalid one (requiring a fresh, complete month), reflecting the juristic preference for certainty in fulfilling religious obligations.
